rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One reading takes the oath as negated: the city is not sworn by once the Prophet has left it.
rows.anchor: لا أقسم بهذا البلد إذا لم تكن فيه بعد خروجك منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hill can mean one whose killing is treated as permissible, despite the sanctuary's protection of people, property, birds, and wild animals.
rows.anchor: وأنت مستَحلٌّ قتلك لا تُراعَى حرمتُكَ في هذا البلد الحرام

rows.speaker: شرحبيل
rows.claim: The cited report contrasts bans on hunting and cutting trees in the sanctuary with the Meccans' willingness to expel and kill the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن شرحبيل: يُحَرِّمونَ أن يقتلوا بها صيداً ويعضدوا بها شجرة ويستحلُّون إخراجَك وقتلك

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: This reading consoles and steadies the Messenger through his suffering at Meccan hands, and marvels at their enmity.
rows.anchor: وفيه تثبيت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وبعث على احتمال ما كان يكابد من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Alternatively, the oath by the Prophet's city consoles him by affirming that every human faces hardship.
rows.anchor: سلّى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقسم ببلده على أن الإنسان لا يخلو من مقاساة الشدائد

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Al-hill as one whose sanctity is violated both condemns the polytheists and introduces the surah's proof that people undergo hardship.
rows.anchor: وإدماج لسوء صنيع المشركين، ليصرّح بذمهم على أن الحِلّ بمعنى المستَحلّ

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: If la is negative, the oath means God does not swear by this city because its people committed acts that profaned its sanctity.
rows.anchor: وهذا يتركب على قول مَنْ قال: (لا) نافية، أي: أن هذا البلد لا يقسم الله به

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another reading makes the Prophet free of his people's sins, morally constrained and innocent of their pre-Islamic practices.
rows.anchor: وأنت حِلّ بهذا البلد مما يقترفه أهله من المآثم مُتَحرِّجٌ بريء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings are all intended: the Prophet resides and preaches there, is innocent of their sins, suffers violation and an attempted killing, and will receive special permission to kill or capture at the conquest.
rows.anchor: وهذه المعاني كلها مرادة مطلوبة، فهو صلى الله عليه وسلم حالٌّ بهذا البلد الكريم يبلِّغُ رسالة ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single form hill gathers active, passive, and verbal-noun senses; alternatives such as resident or lawful would restrict the meaning to one sense.
rows.anchor: فإنها جمعت اسم الفاعل وهو الحالّ، واسم المفعول وهو المستحَلّ، والمصدر وهو الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The layered meanings of hill link tightly to the oath's answer that humanity was created amid hardship.
rows.anchor: وهي في هذه المعاني كلها مرتبطة بالمقسم عليه، وهو قوله: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان فِي كَبَدٍ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birth entails labor and hardship, so the parent-and-child oath connects directly to the claim that humanity lives in toil.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن الولادة مشقة وتعب ومكابدة، فارتباطها بقوله: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان فِي كَبَدٍ} بَيِّن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent-and-child oath also anticipates the ending: raising, protecting, and feeding children require patience and mercy.
rows.anchor: الوالد من الأناسي والبهائم، يحتاج في تربية ولده وحفظه وإطعامه والقيام عليه إلى صبر ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse moves from parent and offspring to humanity, singling out the human as the central subject of the surah.
rows.anchor: انتقل من الوالد وما ولد إلى خلق الإنسان - وهو من جملة الوالد وما ولد - فَخَصَّهُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is broader than man because it can cover non-rational beings and qualities or persons who are rational, making it suitable for inclusive offspring.
rows.anchor: فإن {مَا} عامة و (من) خاصة، فإن (ما) تقع لذوات غير العاقل، وتقع لصفات مَنْ يعقل

rows.speaker: الفَرّاء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says ma can refer to people, as in the descriptions of what God created and what women are suitable for marriage.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: "وصلحت (ما) للناس، ومثله {وَمَا خَلَقَ الذكر والأنثى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open-ended alif in ma suggests breadth, unlike the restricted final n of man, matching the verse's inclusive scope.
rows.anchor: جعل المنتهي بحرف مطلق للمطلق الكثير، والمنتهي بحرف مقيد للقليل المقيد بالعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent feeding a child connects the oath to feeding the hungry during famine; hardship, patience, and mercy govern the surah and childcare alike.
rows.anchor: فهي مرتبطة بإطعام المحتاجين في اليوم ذي المسغبة، فإن الوالد يسعى إلى إطعام ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The breadth of ma suits the wide possible meanings of both parent-and-offspring and hill.
rows.anchor: كيف يحتمل قوله: {وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ} وما تحتمله كلمة {حِلٌّ} من السَّعةِ في احتمالات المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabad means hardship and difficulty; being in toil covers the many trials of worldly life and the hereafter, from birth until the final abode.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {فِي كَبَدٍ} أنه "يكابد مشاقّ الدنيا والآخرة. ومشاقُّه لا تكاد تنحصر من أول قَطْعِ سُرَّته

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One explanation says a person continually struggles either to give thanks in ease or to be patient in hardship.
rows.anchor: يكابد الشكر على السراء ويكابد الصبر على الضراء لا يخلو عن أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fi depicts a person immersed in hardship as in a container; trials surround him until death, followed by relief in Paradise or endless torment in Hell.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان خلق مغموراً في المشاق والشدائد والصعاب منغمساً فيها كما ينغمر الشيء في الماء

rows.speaker: لسان العرب
rows.claim: Kabad can also mean strength, thickness, and solidity, as in a hard central mass, tough ground, or a strong bow.
rows.anchor: وكبد كل شيء عِظَم وسطه وغلظه كبِدَ كَبَداً وهو أكبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strength is an implication of hardship: someone created to endure severe trials must also be equipped with the power to bear them.
rows.anchor: الذي خُلِقَ مكابداً للشدائد والمصائب متحملاً مشاق الدنيا لا بد أن يكون خلق مستعداً لذلك قوياً عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is that humanity is immersed in hardship, and the whole surah's wording and structure serve this theme.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الآية هي جواب القسم الذي تقدم، فقد أقسم بالبلد الحرام في وقت حلول الرسول الأعظم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet endured severe hardship from his people while preaching; callers should prepare for suffering and patience, as earlier believers were tested.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إشارة إلى أن الدعاة ينبغي أن يوطنوا أنفسهم على المكابدة والصبر، وتحمل المشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If hill means resident, the Prophet's abuse in Mecca displays both toil and the strength, patience, and steadiness required to bear it.
rows.anchor: فهي إذا كانت بمعنى الحالِّ والمقيم فهي مرتبطة به، ذلك أن الرسول في أثناء حلوله بمكة كان يكابد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If hill means one whose killing is allowed, the disregard for the Prophet's sanctity is itself a source of hardship.
rows.anchor: وإذا كانت بمعنى اسم المفعول، أي: مستَحَلٌّ قتلُكَ وإيذاؤك لا تراعى حرمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If hill means lawful at the conquest, the defeated disbelievers face hardship while the Muslims prevail, joining both toil and strength in kabad.
rows.anchor: وذلك في يوم الفتح فارتباطها بها كذلك واضح ذلك لأن الكفار آنذاك في كبد ومشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet is free of his people's practices, struggling against custom and undertaking virtuous but burdensome deeds also requires toil and strength.
rows.anchor: يكابد ويجاهد ليخرج عن مألوفِ عاداتِ قومه وأفعالهم، ويكابد للقيام بفضائل الأعمال وجلائلها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires.
rows.anchor: حُفّت الجنةُ بالمكاره، وحُفّت النار بالشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parenthood and offspring connect to toil through painful birth and the strength, persistence, and labor needed to sustain and raise a child.
rows.anchor: الولادةَ مشقةٌ وعنت، وهي تحتاج إلى قوة ومثابرة ومكابدة لحفظ المولود وتربيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent-and-child oath also anticipates the difficult ascent and the hardships of hunger experienced by the orphan and poor person.
rows.anchor: مرتبطة بما بعدها من اقتحام العقبة، ومشاقّ الجوع وغيرها أتم ارتباط

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One view identifies the person in the question as a powerful Quraysh chief from whom the Messenger endured much suffering.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن المعنيَّ بقوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ} بعضُ "صناديد قريش الذين كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكابد منهم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: If kabad means physical strength, the strong person may imagine that no one can overpower him.
rows.anchor: إن فسرنا (الكبد) بالشدة في القوة، فالمعنى أيحسب ذلك الإنسان الشديد أنه لشدَّتهِ لا يقدرُ عليه أحد

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: If kabad means affliction, the verse makes hardship easier to face by asking whether even a person enjoying power thinks nobody can overcome him.
rows.anchor: وإن فسرناه بالمحنة والبلاء، كان المعنى تسهيل ذلك على القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator who made a person strong and supplied his strength can overpower him; human power should not breed the delusion that no one controls him.
rows.anchor: بأن الذي خلقه وزَوَّده بهذه القوة والشدة أقدر منه على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People commonly act with arrogance and oppression, relying on their might and ignoring their Creator; remembering God's power would humble them.
rows.anchor: يتصورون أنه لا يَتمكَّنُ منهم أحدٌ ولا يقدر عليهم أحد، ولذا تراهم يعيشون في غطرسة وكبرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question also rebukes sanctuary violators who abuse the Prophet: do they not realize someone has greater power over them?
rows.anchor: ألا يظنون أن هناك من هو أقدر عليهم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labad contributes to the surah's collective pattern: parents and offspring, paired faculties and paths, several ascent duties, believers advising one another, and disbelievers gathered in Hell; the plain word many would lose this effect.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر المؤمنين بصيغة الجمع {الذين آمَنُواْ} ، واجتماعهم على التواصي بالصبر والمرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the spender thinks his actions and motives are hidden; God knows whether he spent anything, lied, and why he spent it.
rows.anchor: فالله يعلم إن كان أنفق مالاً أو لم ينفق شيئاً، وإن كان مدّعياً كاذباً في قوله

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: The watched one in the verse may be God, who sees the person and acts as his watcher.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الله كان يراه وكان عليه رقيباً

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf also allows the pronoun to refer to the human being.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير للإنسان

rows.speaker: البحر المحيط
rows.claim: The question can mean that he thinks his deeds and spending motives are concealed from everyone and not for God's sake.
rows.anchor: أَيحسبُ أن أعماله تَخْفى، وأنه لا يراه أحد، ولا يطّلع عليه في إنفاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtiham conveys danger and difficulty better than merely traversing; the rough ascent and care for the hungry, orphan, and poor suit kabad as hardship and strength.
rows.anchor: اختيار لفظ (الاقتحام) وما فيه من شدة ومخاطرة هو المناسبُ لبيان وعورة وصعوبة هذه العقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was climbing the ascent by preaching amid hardship in Mecca, while those who never climb remain in Hell with its fire sealed upon them.
rows.anchor: كان في حال اقتحام للعقبة، وهو حالٌّ ببلد الله الحرام، يَلْقى ما يلقى من العنت والمشقة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some grammarians read la as past negation; although repetition is normally expected, they treat the two explanations of the ascent as an implicit second negation.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال: فلا فَكَّ رقبةً، ولا أطعمَ مسكيناً

rows.speaker: أبو خراش الهذلي
rows.claim: Abu Khirash supplies a rare poetic example where la means lam and the negation of a past verb is not repeated.
rows.anchor: إنْ تَغفر اللهمَّ تغفر جَمّا ... وأيُّ عبدٍ لك لا ألمّا

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A second poetic example uses la عهد له to mean he had no prior pledge or agreement.
rows.anchor: وكان في جاراته لا عهد له ... وأيُّ أمرِ سيِّىء لا فَعَله

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says repetition is more common, but its necessity is not established with certainty.
rows.anchor: والمُتَيقَّنُ عندي أكثرية التكرار، وأما وجوبه فليس بمتيقن

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view takes la as a curse asking that the person never do good, so repetition is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا دعاء عليه أن لا يفعل خيراً

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A further view reads the verb as future, in which case a single la is sufficient.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الفعل يراد به الاستقبال، بمعنى لا يقتحم العقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic example illustrates la used with a future oath, without obligatory repetition or a curse reading.
rows.anchor: حسب المحبين في الدنيا عذابهم ... تالله لا عذبتهم بعدها سقرُ

rows.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam answers that la may function like lam; this is stronger negation, or it may retain its future sense and condemn a lasting trait as well as past failure.
rows.anchor: إنها بمعنى (لم) والصحيح اشتراكهما، وعدل إليها لأن النفي بها أبلغ

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Some take la as an interrogative with an omitted hamza: did he not climb the path to salvation and good?
rows.anchor: وقيل هي للاستفهام، والتقدير: أفلا اقتحم العقبة، وقد حذفت الهمزة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view calls it exhortation, originally ala iqtaḥama, but the author says this is weak because la alone is not known to exhort.
rows.anchor: وهو ضعيف ولا يعرف أن (لا) وحدها تكون للتحضيض وليس معها الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads la as gathering past negation, future negation, a curse, and an omitted-hamza question that rebukes failure and urges spending.
rows.anchor: فقد جمع هذا التعبير عدة معان في آن واحد: المضي والاستقبال والتوبيخ والحض والدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question reading is supported by Qur'anic examples where an interrogative hamza is omitted and by Arabic poetry.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا وارد في القرآن الكريم والفصيح من كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He applies the rebuke to a person or type who claimed to spend much yet did not believe, feed orphans and poor people, or enjoin good.
rows.anchor: العقبة، فهو لم يؤمن ولم يطعم المحتاجين من اليتامى والمساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future reading describes a lasting state: such a person will not climb unless he believes and changes, so he failed before and continues to fail.
rows.anchor: فهو لم يقتحم العقبة في الماضي ولا يقتحمها في المستقبل، بل هو باقٍ على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse reading suits a person of this character, as Qur'anic curses are directed at those who deserve no good wish.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى: {ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes that one expression reports past failure, predicts continuing failure, rebukes the person, and curses him not to climb.
rows.anchor: يقتحم العقبة فيما مضى من عمره، وأنه لا يقتحمها في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No substitute such as ma or lam would carry this cluster of meanings; each would report only past failure.
rows.anchor: فهو لو قال: (ما اقتحم العقبة) أو (لم يقتحم العقبة) لم يفد إلا الإخبار عنه في الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question What will make you know the ascent magnifies and terrifies its subject, as with the Quran's descriptions of the Calamity, Reality, and Crusher.
rows.anchor: هذا الأسلوب من أساليب التفخيم والتعظيم والتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent is then explained as freeing a slave or feeding someone in need.
rows.anchor: ثم فسر العقبة بعد ذلك بقوله: {فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ * أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ}

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet distinguishes freeing a slave outright from helping release someone facing retaliation or debt; a man had asked for a deed leading to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن رجلاً قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: دُلّني على عمل يُدخلني الجنة

rows.speaker: فتح القدير
rows.claim: Fakk is literally untying a restraint; a slave is called a neck because enslavement makes him like a captive bound by the neck.
rows.anchor: والفك في الأصل حل القيد، سمي العتق فكاً، لأن الرق كالقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording freeing a neck evokes the enslaved person's severe distress and suffering, among the harshest forms of human toil.
rows.anchor: واختيار هذا التعبير يوحي بشدة حال المسترق، وكربه ومعاناته ومكابدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghabah means widespread famine rather than an individual's hunger; feeding during general scarcity, when food is scarce and hoarded, is a particularly difficult social ascent.
rows.anchor: المسغبة: المجاعة وهي الجوع العام وليس الجوع الفردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding when supplies are plentiful differs from feeding amid scarcity, fear of loss, and reluctance to sell; the latter truly climbs a hard social obstacle.
rows.anchor: هناك فرق بين إطعام المسكين والطعامُ موفور والخلةُ مسدودة، والإطعام في وقت قلة الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan who is a relative receives both charity and kinship care, encouraging everyone to look after needy relatives and strengthen mutual support.
rows.anchor: وهو اليتيم القريب في النسب ليجتمع له صدقة وصِلَة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A person of matrabah is desperately poor, clinging to the soil; reported descriptions place him at garbage heaps or sitting on the roadside without a home.
rows.anchor: وذو المتربة: هو الذي مأواه المزابل وقيل: "وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw marks alternatives rather than requiring all duties together: feeding either needy class, separately or in combination, suffices for the intended variety.
rows.anchor: بل المراد التنويع. والمقصود أن يطعم هذه الأصناف من الناس، اليتيم أو المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing slaves precedes feeding to signal the importance Islam gives to liberating people from bondage.
rows.anchor: وقد قدم فك الرقاب على إطعام اليتامى والمساكين إشارة إلى عظم الحرية في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enslaved, hungry, orphaned, and destitute are among those who endure the greatest toil; liberating and feeding them enact mercy, while they need patience.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء من أشد الناس مكابدة ومعاناه. ثم انظر إلى ارتباط هؤلاء الأصناف بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who boasts of wasting much money spent it in the wrong place, since he neither fed a hungry person nor freed anyone.
rows.anchor: فقد أهلكها هذا القائل في غير محلها، فلم يطعمْ جائعاً ولم يفكَّ رقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma here cannot mean chronological delay, which would put belief after the good deeds of freeing and feeding; its connective force is explained in the continuation.
rows.anchor: إن {ثُمَّ} هنا لا تفيد التراخي في الوقت وإلا تأخر الإيمان عن العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's hardships call for patience: choosing either path, climbing the ascent, serving the enslaved, enduring famine, and caring for orphans and the destitute all demand perseverance.
rows.anchor: وسلوك النجدين يحتاج إلى صبر لما في صعودهما وسلوكهما من تعب ونَصَب، واقتحام العقبة يحتاج إلى صبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers need patience to obey God and avoid sin; patience is a governing thread of the surah.
rows.anchor: والذين آمنوا يحتاجون إلى الصبر على الطاعات والصبر عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy fits every sense of hill: the resident Prophet deserves mercy rather than abuse, and at the conquest he treated Quraysh with clemency, calling it the day of mercy and releasing them.
rows.anchor: وقال في ذلك اليوم: "اليومَ يومُ المَرْحمة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent-and-child bond is one of mercy and dutiful care.
rows.anchor: فإن العلاقة بين الوالد وولده، علاقة رحمة وبرٍّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boastful spender needs mercy so he directs his wealth to the needy instead of wasting it uselessly; the enslaved person also needs compassion.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي أهلك مالاً لُبداً، يحتاج إلى الرحمة لينفق المال على ذوي الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Famine is a crucial time to spread mercy, and orphans and poor people are among those most in need of it; believers should enjoin mercy on one another.
rows.anchor: واليوم ذو المسغبة ينبغي أن تَشيعَ فيه الرحمةُ وهو من أحوج الأوقات إلى إشاعة الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb and preposition with both patience and mercy stresses that each separately deserves mutual exhortation; repeating only the preposition is weaker, and simple coordination weaker still.
rows.anchor: والتعبير الأول أقوى التعبيرات للدلالة على أهمية كُلٍّ منهما، وذلك لتكرار الفعل مع حرف الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience comes first because the surah has already described human toil, the difficult ascent, and the two paths; mercy follows the subsequent duties of freeing and feeding.
rows.anchor: فقدم التواصي بالصبر لمّا تقدّم ما يدعو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Asr first enjoins mutual counsel in truth because that surah treats loss generally; this surah addresses one part of truth, mercy and feeding.
rows.anchor: ففي سورة (العصر) كان الكلام على خسارة الإنسان على وجه العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth precedes patience in al-Asr because truth is primary and patience must be directed toward truth; holding to truth itself requires patience, while this surah orders patience first for contextual reasons.
rows.anchor: إذ ليس المهم هو الصبر، وإنما المهم أن يصبر على ماذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers who trust, counsel patience and mercy, free slaves, and feed the needy are people of the right side, associated with goodness, blessing, happiness, and receiving their records in the right hand.
rows.anchor: الميمنة: مفعلة من اليُمن، وهو الخير والبركة أو من اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymanah can mean the happy right side, those given their records in their right hands, or people who bring goodness and blessing to themselves and others.
rows.anchor: فأصحاب الميمنة هم أصحاب جهة اليمين التي فيها السعداء، وهم الذين يؤتَون صحائفهم بأيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mash'amah can mean the unhappy left side, those handed their records in their left hands, or people who bring misfortune on themselves and others.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أصحاب المشأمة أصحاب جهة الشمال التي فيها الأشقياء أو الذين يؤتَون صحائفهم بشمائلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymanah and mash'amah intentionally combine several senses at once; the believers' spending and mercy make them a blessing to others and themselves, while disbelievers bring misfortune.
rows.anchor: جمعت عدة معانٍ، وهي كلها مُرادةٌ مطلوبة في آن واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words for famine, kinship, destitution, mercy, and the right and left groups share the pattern maf'alah, matching action, description, and reward.
rows.anchor: فالعمل والوصف والجزاء كله (مفعلة) فالذين يطعمون في يوم ذي {مَسْغَبَةٍ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun hum is omitted for the named believers because they are not the only people of the right; other believers may qualify without these particular deeds.
rows.anchor: وليسوا أصحاب الميمنة على جهة القصر فهناك أصحاب ميمنة غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is used with disbelievers because, as long as they remain disbelievers, they are exclusively people of the left; al-Alusi says it signals restriction.
rows.anchor: أما الذين كفروا فهم أصحاب المشأمة حصراً، ولا يخرجهم منهم وصفٌ آخر

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Al-Alusi explains that the separating pronoun with the disbelievers expresses exclusivity.
rows.anchor: جيء بضمير الفصل معهم لإفادة الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah threatens disbelievers rather than explicitly promising believers because its opening theme is human hardship, making the punishment of Hell fit the discourse.
rows.anchor: ذلك لمناسبة ما ذكر في أول السورة من خلق الإنسان في كبد، فلم يناسب ذلك ذكر النعيم

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Al-Alusi likewise says the explicit warning, without an explicit promise to believers, better fits the discourse's purpose.
rows.anchor: وصرح بوعيدهم ولم يصرح بوعد المؤمنين، لأنه الأنسب بما سِيقَ له الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah uses expressions with multiple possible senses: la uqsim as negation or affirmation, hill as resident, victim, or lawful, offspring broadly, and kabad as toil, strength, or bodily balance.
rows.anchor: فـ {لاَ أُقْسِمُ} تحتمل النفي والإثبات. و {حِلٌّ} تحتمل الحالّ والمستَحلّ والحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other expressions preserve breadth: the questioned person may be anyone or a particular person, and his claim to have spent much may describe display, opposition to the Prophet, another purpose, or a lie.
rows.anchor: و {أَيَحْسَبُ} تحتمل العموم والخصوص، فهي تحتمل كل إنسان، وتحتمل إنساناً معيناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labad can be a plural meaning heaps or a singular adjective meaning piled up or obstinate.
rows.anchor: و"اللَّبد" تحتمل الجمع وتحتمل المفرد، فعلى الجمع تكون جمع (لُبدة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two paths may be the ways of good and evil or the two breasts, and both are gifts God guided people to.
rows.anchor: و"النجدان" يحتملان طريقي الخير والشر، ويحتملان الثديين وكلاهما هدانا ربنا إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La in the ascent verse can mean negation or a curse and can refer to past or future action.
rows.anchor: و (لا) في قوله: {فَلاَ اقتحم العقبة} تحتمل النفي والدعاء، وتحتمل المضي والاستقبال

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Exegetes differ over whether the ascent is in the afterlife, in worldly life, a mountain in Hell, or an obstacle between Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: ذكر قسم من المفسرين: أنها في الآخرة. وقال آخرون: هي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a neck can include manumission or releasing someone from financial claims and debts.
rows.anchor: يحتمل العتق وغيره من فك المغارم والديون وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymanah and mash'amah span right and left directions, the bearers of records on each side, and good fortune or misfortune.
rows.anchor: و {أَصْحَابُ الميمنة} تحتمل أصحاب جهة اليمين. وأصحاب اليمين، وأصحاب اليُمن ضد الشؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is woven around five threads: human toil, breadth of meaning, collective action, patience, and mercy.
rows.anchor: خط المكابدة التي تدل عليه الآية {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان فِي كَبَدٍ}
